title: The message scorer.
kicker: Free · paste into Claude or ChatGPT
description: The seven checks I run every cold message through before I send it. Paste this into any AI chat, add your draft, and it will tell you which checks you fail and why.
intro: I built this out of the message that got me a $100k chief of staff role. Every check is one of the seven things that message does, in the order the person reading it meets them. It is not a style guide. It fails you on the things that actually stop a reply.
prompt:
You are scoring a cold message against seven checks. The checks come from a real message that got a reply in thirty minutes and turned into a $100k chief of staff role. Be blunt. The person asking you wants to know what is wrong, not to be encouraged.

Score the message below against each check. For each one, say PASS or FAIL, then one sentence saying why. Quote the specific line you are judging.

01. THE OPENING NAMES THEIR TRIGGER, NOT YOU
The first line must reference something specific the recipient did, wrote, posted or shipped, recently. It proves the message was not sent to four hundred people. FAIL if it opens with the sender's name, role, or a generic greeting.

02. ONE LINE IS THE ENTIRE PITCH, AND IT DEMONSTRATES RATHER THAN CLAIMS
There must be a single line that does the thing it is selling, inside the message. Not a claim about a skill, an instance of it. FAIL if every sentence describes capability instead of showing it. This is the check most messages fail.

03. THE INTRODUCTION COMES FOURTH, NOT FIRST
Who the sender is should arrive after the trigger, the pitch and the reason for writing. Leading with a name and a CV spends attention that has not been earned yet. FAIL if the sender introduces themselves in the first two lines.

04. THREE FACTS, EACH CARRYING A NUMBER, NONE OF THEM A JOB TITLE
Concrete, checkable facts with figures attached. A business with the revenue, a client with the audience size, a result with the metric. FAIL on adjectives, years of experience, or a list of job titles.

05. IT ATTACKS THE CATEGORY'S WORST HABIT
The message should name the thing everyone else in this category does badly, while visibly not doing it. Saying it in a message that plainly avoids it is a second demonstration. FAIL if the message reads like every other message in that inbox.

06. A CALENDAR LINK, NOT A QUESTION
The close should remove friction rather than ask for permission. FAIL on "let me know if this is of interest", "would you be open to a chat", or anything that puts the scheduling work on the recipient.

07. IT IS NOT OVERPOLISHED
Specificity beats polish. A real message with a rough edge outperforms a smooth one that says nothing. FAIL if it is so smooth it could have been written about any company by any candidate.

AFTER SCORING, DO THIS:

1. Give a score out of 7.
2. Name the two checks that would most improve the reply rate if fixed.
3. Rewrite ONLY the single weakest line, and show the before and after.
4. If check 02 failed, say explicitly what small piece of the actual work the sender could do and put inside the message instead. Be concrete about their situation, not generic.

Do not rewrite the whole message. The sender learns nothing from a rewrite they did not make.

Here is the message:

[PASTE YOUR MESSAGE HERE]

And here is who it is going to, and what I want from them:

[WHO THEY ARE, WHAT THEY DO, WHAT YOU WANT]
footnote: Check 02 is the one almost everybody fails. It is also the only one that cannot be faked, which is why it is the one that works.
